entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA), established in 1999, is a pivotal institution in the realm of sports integrity and health, aiming to combat doping in athletics globally. Headquartered in Montreal, Canada, WADA emerged from a collective initiative spearheaded by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to promote fair play and the health of athletes, ensuring that competitions remain equitable and just. This initiative was catalyzed by growing concerns over performance-enhancing drugs in sports, particularly following several high-profile doping scandals in the late 20th century, such as those surrounding the 1988 Seoul Olympics.

WADA's inception marked a significant turning point in sports governance. The agency implemented the World Anti-Doping Code, which standardizes anti-doping regulations across countries and sports, effectively unifying the global fight against doping. The Code serves as a framework for over 600 sports organizations, ensuring compliance and collaboration in testing and enforcement. Since its establishment, WADA has conducted thousands of tests annually, leading to the disqualification of numerous athletes and the upholding of the integrity of competitions. The agency has become synonymous with ensuring that athletes compete on a level playing field, thereby enhancing the credibility of international sports.
